subject: Evidence logbook: subprocessor chaining, dataflow logs, and KMS proof
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@mediacorp.com>
To: priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Singh <b.singh@healthgrid.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Info request: logs and subprocessor chain for PII telemetry

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — Medi aCorp's security team had two follow-ups they asked me to get clarified before the pilot goes live:

1) We need an "evidence logbook" that shows how PII-related telemetry flows through Redwood's stack end-to-end, including any subprocessor handoffs (names, purpose, region). A simple timeline/table will work.
2) For dataflow logs, we want to see what logging is retained (access logs, request metadata) and the retention windows for those logs for both hosted and dedicated deployments.
3) KMS proof: can you supply a short attestation (or pointer to existing artifact) that describes key custody for customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed keys? The security reviewer is specific about chain-of-custody language.

Bob from HealthGrid suggested you might already have a small template we can populate. Could you send the logbook and any attestation stubs by EOD Wednesday PST?

Appreciate it — we want to close this before the legal review.

Best,
Alice Turner
Security Lead, Medi aCorp

From: priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@mediacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Info request: logs and subprocessor chain for PII telemetry

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick note to confirm scope before we assemble artifacts:

- "PII telemetry" in your context = user-generated prompts + any user identifiers attached to requests. Please confirm if you also want low-level runtime telemetry (GPU traces / infer logs) — we usually treat that as operational and redact identifiers.
- Do you want separate evidence for Hosted API vs Dedicated (reserved pools)? We have slightly different retention defaults and subprocessor mapping for each.

Plan: we will: 1) produce a concise logbook PDF that enumerates the processors and subprocessors (purpose, region, legal basis), 2) attach a short KMS attestation stub that explains custody and rotation, and 3) produce a table of relevant logs and retention windows. I will pull the initial drafts and share with the internal privacy owners for review.

Deliverable ETA: draft logbook + KMS stub and logs table by Wed 18:00 PST. If you confirm the scope (prompts + identifiers only), we'll proceed that way.

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@mediacorp.com>
To: priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Singh <b.singh@healthgrid.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Info request: logs and subprocessor chain for PII telemetry

On Mon, 16 Nov 2026 at 11:03, priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick note to confirm scope before we assemble artifacts:
>
> - "PII telemetry" in your context = user-generated prompts + any user identifiers attached to requests. Please confirm if you also want low-level runtime telemetry (GPU traces / infer logs) — we usually treat that as operational and redact identifiers.
>
Yes, prompts and associated identifiers are the priority. We do not need GPU traces — only request/response metadata and access logs where identifiers appear. The security reviewer flagged two specific items: a) whether request IDs are present in subprocessor logs, and b) whether any cross-region transfer happens when fallbacks route to warm spare capacity (we need the decision tree).

If you can include clear examples in the logbook (e.g., pseudo-rows showing a request travel path and which subprocessors saw which fields), that will make legal and security happy.

Thanks — we'll expect the draft Wed EOD.

Alice

From: priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@mediacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence logbook: subprocessor chaining, dataflow logs, and KMS proof

Alice — attaching the draft artifacts per your asks (see attachment stubs below). Summary of what we included:

- dataflow_logbook_v1.pdf (attached): concise timeline + table of processors and subprocessors, purpose, region, and whether PII fields are observable. The logbook includes two example pseudo-rows showing a request path with which components see identifiers.
- kms_attestation_stub.txt (attached): short custody statement for Redwood-managed keys and instructions/expectations for customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Logs table (in the PDF): enumerates retained logs (access logs, request metadata, audit trail) and retention defaults (Hosted: 90 days access logs, 30 days request payload index; Dedicated: configurable via contract, default 365 days for audit trail).
- Routing/fallback note: warm spare routing can cross regions only when a customer has not pinned region/tier; we documented the decision tree and the automatic opt-out knob (region_pin in deployment config).

Open items we flagged for internal review: 1) redaction examples for request IDs in third-party subprocessors (we recommend tokenization on export), and 2) whether to add a short signed attestation vs the current unsigned stub (legal usually requests a signed artifact for enterprise contracts).

Next steps: Karthik and Marissa will review the logbook language and confirm the subprocessor list. Ben will follow up on the formal attestation cadence. We'll send a cleaned package with any redactions or signed attestation by Friday COB if required.

Attachments (stubs):
- dataflow_logbook_v1.pdf (diagram + tables)
- kms_attestation_stub.txt (1 page)

Let us know if this format works or if your security reviewer wants a different artifact layout.

Thanks —
Priyom

-- 
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
